items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: We had Rika Ellis. And we had William Padua. ... I beat Rika Ellis critics because he's better. He's better. ... He wasn't a good drummer. ... His wife quit him. ... We were playing and she counted my horse. And he said, man, he got up and left the band.

ctx.x: I asked him which came first.

We had some band, too. Most of our jobs called for white people. We said. We was up three years before we could play for one color people. And the first time we played for color people when Joe Oliver left from the air. You know, the thing I got in there when I was standing right by Joe Oliver with a fellow drumming him, Buddy Sali. Hit him in the eye with a wheel by the hammer. And you know, I thought Joe would be one eye, you know. And he used to have a man, Carol, all them boys. He must have been around about…
I asked you who this Bourne was. That's not Harrison Bourne.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: And that's where I told them we had Maurice and, uh, Rika Ellis.

ctx.x: I'll say. I'll say. I'll say.

I'll say. I'll say. I'll say. My band was still up then. And that's where I told them we had Maurice and, uh, Rika Ellis. I'll say. Rika Ellis. Rika Ellis. I don't know why Rika left us, but we got, uh, uh, Maurice here. He just come from World of War, you know. First World of War, you know. And then he got in and I'm going to start the bossing, you know. And we said, yeah, we're all young boys, you know, get a band over in the community, try to run all bands along as we've been up. And that's why we kept on and…
I used to lead it for him to catch it. He said, when he catch it, he had a good laugh.
